title: Test the spirits (1 John 4:1–6)
hookLine: not every voice is from God; test it

cards: Before there were labs, people tested gold by rubbing it on a dark stone and looking at the streak it left. Real gold left one color. Fakes left another.

The stone was called a touchstone, and its lesson was simple: something can look exactly like gold and not be gold. Today the writer of First John turns brisk and practical: don't believe every voice. Test it.

teach.b: In the King James Bible: "Beloved, believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God: because many false prophets are gone out into the world."
Try translates a Greek word also used for testing metal, an assayer's word. And he starts with beloved: not a cynic, but someone who loves his readers enough to want them not to be fooled.
In his day, it seems, teachers were claiming the Spirit, and some said that Jesus didn't really come in a body.

teach.h: DID JESUS COME IN THE FLESH?
teach.b: So his test fits his moment: "Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God." Remember the letter's opening: what our hands have handled.
The test is whether a teaching holds on to a real, touchable Jesus.

teach.h: GREATER IS HE THAT IS IN YOU.
teach.b: Then courage: "greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world." The reader isn't small and helpless before every persuasive voice. And a sobering line: the world listens to its own.
Popular doesn't mean true. Christians call this gift discernment; Paul lists the discerning of spirits among the Spirit's gifts.
Churches have taught many ways to practice it. Catholic and Orthodox teaching weighs a claim against Scripture read with the church's tradition.
Protestant teaching holds Scripture as the final test, often weighed with the counsel of a community. Ignatius of Loyola wrote rules for discerning the spirits that are still taught today.
Each starts where the writer does: some voices sound like gold, so test them before trusting them.

how: Christians practice discernment by testing teachings against Scripture and the faith of the church, and some seek the help of a pastor, spiritual director or community; Ignatian discernment, from Ignatius of Loyola, is still taught today.

games.q: a confident teacher arrives claiming the Spirit, and says Jesus never really had a body. what does the letter say to do?
o: test the spirit: does it confess Jesus Christ come in the flesh?
games.why: "Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God." test before you trust.

practice: Think of one thing you accepted quickly this week, a headline, a rumor, a confident voice, even an inner voice about yourself, and hold it up like gold on a touchstone.
Where did it come from, who benefits if you believe it, does it lead toward love or away from it? Don't rush to a verdict, and if you pray, ask for discernment.

wordCard.voice: Discernment. The gift of testing voices before trusting them, the way a touchstone tells real gold from fake.

orig.note: Greek: to test, assay, prove, as with metals. the word behind 'try the spirits'.
